verdict.summary: The global payments gateway feature collects card details and potentially other payment-related data from customers worldwide, with some AI involvement in payment processing. The collected data aligns with the legislative excerpts provided, which includes Regulation E for error refunds and GDPR for explicit consent, but there are unclear aspects that need clarification.

issues.title: Lack of specific AI impact on payment processing
issues.description: The exact role and influence of the AI component in the payment processing decisions within the app are not fully specified or clarified.
issues.impact: Potential non-compliance with local regulations related to AI in payment processing decisions.
issues.remediation: Clearly document the role and influence of AI in payment processing decisions within the app.

issues.title: Unclear geo-specific legal concerns
issues.description: There is a lack of clarity regarding potential geo-specific legal concerns that may impact the payments gateway feature, such as local data protection laws in various jurisdictions where users reside.
issues.impact: Potential legal risks and non-compliance with local regulations due to unclear geo-specific legal concerns.
issues.remediation: Identify and address potential geo-specific legal concerns related to the payments gateway feature, such as local data protection laws in various jurisdictions.

evidence_cited.content: Requires financial institutions to provide prompt refunds for errors in electronic fund transfers.
Requires explicit consent for collecting and storing personal data of EU citizens.
